title: Understanding Codons
text: Think about how DNA is structured. Each sequence of three letters forms a codon, which is crucial for encoding amino acids. How might this influence your choice of encoding strategy?

title: Compactness vs. Meaning
text: Consider the trade-off between compactness and preserving the meaning of the data. Why might a more compact representation not always be the best choice?

hintAnswer: One hot encode each of the 1,000 disjoint codons, per sample.
title: Choosing the Right Encoding
text: Which encoding strategy allows you to capture the unique sequences of three letters that are crucial for protein synthesis?
choices: Apply one one hot encoding to the entire DNA string.
One hot encode each of the 1,000 disjoint codons, per sample.
One hot encode each of the $$500$$ disjoint $$6$$ letter combinations, per sample.
Bag of words encoding, where each "word" is a codon
